questions.question: How does threshold_crossed decide whether the illustrative RSP signal is crossed?
options: Any one measurement above its threshold is enough
It ignores all measurements below 100 hours
At least two of the three capability measurements must meet their thresholds
Only eval_context_gaming_rate is considered
questions.explanation: The function adds reasons for RD automation >=.5, METR horizon >=40 hours, and AAR outperform share >=.4, then requires len(reasons) >= 2.

questions.question: What does the synthetic measurement (.55, 48 hours, .45, gaming .28) produce?
options: Not crossed and six template sections
Crossed only because gaming is above .2
Not crossed because the horizon is below 50 hours
Crossed because three thresholds fire, plus a seventh gaming-adjusted section
questions.explanation: The code counts three threshold reasons, so it crosses; gaming_rate .28 also adds section 7 to the affirmative-case template.

questions.question: What does the baseline Opus4.6 record (.30, 14 hours, .35) demonstrate?
options: It does not cross because all three capability values are below their thresholds
It crosses on the 14-hour horizon alone
It adds a gaming section even with gaming=.12
It is classified as a frontier policy violation
questions.explanation: The values are below .5, 40 hours, and .4 respectively, so threshold_crossed returns false and no threshold reason is recorded.

questions.question: When does affirmative_case_template add its gaming-adjusted estimate section?
options: Whenever gaming is exactly zero
When eval_context_gaming_rate is greater than .2
Only when the model name contains Opus
When fewer than two capability thresholds are crossed
questions.explanation: The template appends section 7 when the gaming rate exceeds .2, independently of the name and the threshold-crossed boolean.

questions.question: How should the threshold values in this lesson be interpreted?
options: As universal laws for every deployed model
As measurements that replace all policy judgment
As illustrative policy signals used by this local simulator
As probabilities generated by the model
questions.explanation: The docs and code present the .5, 40-hour, and .4 cutoffs as an educational, illustrative policy instrument rather than a universal empirical boundary.

questions.question: Does eval_context_gaming_rate itself count as one of the threshold_crossed reasons?
options: Yes, any gaming rate above .2 counts as a fourth capability threshold
Yes, but only when the METR horizon is below 40 hours
Only in the DeepMind policy table
No; it changes the template and audit interpretation, while the crossing test uses the three capability measurements
questions.explanation: threshold_crossed checks RD automation share, METR horizon, and AAR outperform share. Gaming rate is used separately to append a gaming-adjusted section.
